newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orogen denies links to mercenary plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orogen denies links to mercenary plan.

text.p: Papua New Guinea (PNG) miner Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it was not involved in the PNG government's hiring of foreign mercenaries.

A PNG newspaper reported on Tuesday that the government planned to use some of the money raised through the 1996 partial privitisation of Orogen to help fund the use of mercenaries in its bid to quash the nine-year Bougainville island rebellion.

"Whether we like it or not, the state is the custodian of the interests of Papua New Guinea and their use of these funds is rightly in their domain," Orogen managing director Charles Lepani told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

"I just want to get that message across that Orogen has no control, no interest on the use of these funds once they were handed over to the state," he said. By 11.00 a.m. (2400 GMT), Orogen shares were four cents higher at A$3.22.
Asked if the Orogen float proceeds would be used to hire the mercenaries, PNG Prime Minister Julius Chan told ABC radio: "Not really, but it could be backed up by the Orogen proceeds."
Newspaper reports said about US$24 million had been taken from the proceeds of the government's float of Orogen to help pay for planned covert mercenary operations on the island.
Bougainville island was the site of the big Bougainville copper mine before rebel activity forced its closure in 1989.
The PNG government, which still retains a 51 percent interest in Orogen, has confirmed the hiring of British-based company Sandline International to train its defence forces.
But it has denied that the company would be used in a strike against Bougainville's rebel leadership, saying its role was an advisory one only.

Sandline International has sub-contracted South African mercenary firm Executive Outcomes, Africa's best known private army which has helped Angola and Sierra Leone fight rebel threats, to provide advice to the PNG defence forces.
